lexical.anchor: G-22/MT-1 has stood since the measure-theory phase: no probability space exists in this theory. It is the gate on every quantitative match 17 tested -- CUSUM, Lyapunov, mixtures, calibration. Three distinct prior verdicts, not the same verdict: a measurable space (Omega,F) for knowledge -- proposed in v0.1, then challenged, but the challenge says the framework can be REPAIRED without abandoning your core idea. 'knowledge projection = measure' -- REFUTED as a primitive. 'Knowledge Space is inherently ONE probability space' -- DECLINED, §18 retains one probability space per probabilistic regime, because semantic concepts do not automatically collapse into a stochastic probability space without losing semantics. The measurable space was never rejected. What was rejected is projection=measure, and what was DECLINED is a single universal P.

rationale_evidence.statement: Provides the precise historical audit trail behind G-22 ('no probability space'): three distinct prior verdicts exist, not one -- a measurable space (Omega,F) was proposed then challenged but judged repairable without abandoning the core idea; 'projection=measure' was refuted as a primitive; and 'Knowledge Space is inherently ONE probability space' was explicitly DECLINED by an earlier §18 in favor of one probability space per probabilistic regime, since semantic concepts do not collapse into a stochastic space without losing semantics. rationale_evidence.anchor: Where the new proposal lands: re-asserts a single universal P -- the universal knowledge possibility space -- but §18 declined exactly this, and the proposal does not cite §18. Does NOT claim projection=measure -- avoids the refuted primitive. Asks the repair question outright: a knowledge element can be modelled as an outcome, random variable, event, measurable function, or probability distribution -- but we must decide which one.
